tagline: Along the crest, between the bay and the ocean.
intro: Skyline Boulevard comes into San Mateo County on the crest of the Santa Cruz Mountains near Long Ridge, at about 2,600 feet the highest ground in the county, and keeps to the ridge for some twenty-three miles north. For most of the way both San Francisco Bay and the Pacific are in view. Open space preserves line it one after another. At Highway 92 the ridgetop road gives out, because the hills beyond are San Francisco's watershed.
On weekends sports cars and motorcycles gather where Highway 84 crosses. The Kings Mountain volunteer fire brigade answers more than 160 calls a year, many of them for cyclists and hikers.

moments.title: Russian Ridge Open Space Preserve
moments.text: Named for a Russian immigrant who ran a dairy here on land leased from San Francisco's mayor. Borel Hill, at 2,572 feet, looks across the bay and out to the Pacific.

moments.title: Windy Hill
moments.text: The one unforested stretch of the peninsula range, its summit half a mile up from the road. In winter, when the east winds blow, paragliders take off from it by permit.

moments.title: Sky Londa
moments.text: A crossroads hamlet at 1,520 feet. Maps as early as 1909 spell it Sky L'onda, apparently from the two roads that meet here, Skyline and La Honda.
